newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Waigel warns against softening EMU deficit target.
newsitem.headline: Waigel warns against softening EMU deficit target.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that allowing a nation to qualify for European monetary union (EMU) with a deficit of 3.3 percent of gross domestic product would pave the way for other nations to qualify with even higher deficit overshoots.
"Whoever says 3.3 percent will in the end land at more than four percent in other countries and that is not acceptable," Waigel told reporters ahead of a meeting of European Union finance ministers.

He was responding to question on whether he agreed with the stance of the head of Germany's bank association, Martin Kohlhaussen. In a newspaper interview published at the weekend, Kohlhaussen said that countries should be allowed to qualify with deficit ratios above 3.0 percent.
"There's one figure in the treaty and that is three percent," Waigel said.
